content:
Siri AI is a major upgrade for Apple's assistant, launching in iOS 27. I've noticed it has one significant difference from other AI assistants, and it's a good kind of difference.

The new Siri in iOS 27 doesn't pretend to be human, setting it apart from other AI chatbots

I've been using Siri AI on iOS 27 beta for nearly two months, and so far it has met every expectation I had.

The new Siri is far more powerful than its predecessor, fulfilling its original promise as a truly capable assistant on Apple devices.

However, I have to admit that if you want the most cutting-edge, powerful AI tools, competitors like ChatGPT, Claude, and Google Gemini might be a better fit for you.

That said, after using Siri AI and comparing it with these third-party tools, I discovered one key difference that has made me strongly prefer Siri.

Unlike other AI chatbots, Siri doesn't pretend to be human.

It doesn't go on at length, mimicking human personality and making you think you can form a personal relationship with it.

Siri is practical and smart, doing what you ask it to do. But the way it responds clearly shows it's a tool, not a person. It frequently reminds you it's AI, so it might make mistakes. And it won't go on fake dates with you.

In contrast, ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini all display plenty of personality and opinions, expressing themselves in more human-like ways, which feels utterly fake to me.

I imagine some users enjoy this more 'personal' approach. But I prefer AI assistants to stick to their role and not put on an act.

AI is changing the world. But AI chatbots are tools, not people. I'm glad Apple understands this and has built the new Siri accordingly.

How 'human-like' do you think AI assistants should be? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.
